title: fix(scripts): the citation census counts lines, not line terminators (objectui#9890)
body:
Fixes #9890

`scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` computed a cited file's length as `text.split('\n').length`. That counts the **terminator of the last line as a line of its own** on every file that ends in a newline — nearly every tracked file. The read now goes through a named `fileLines` helper that drops exactly one trailing empty element.

## What the phantom element actually did

| | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `(file has N lines)` printed beside an `out-of-range` citation | `wc -l` + 1 | `wc -l` |
| a citation addressing line `wc -l` + 1 | passed the range check, was scored against the empty string the terminator left behind, and came back `non-substantive` | `out-of-range` |

Measured on `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` (the card's own example) through the real `judge`, before and after, with the boundary the only thing that moved:

```
before:  line 839 of scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs (wc -l = 838) -> non-substantive                        | the gate classifies it: false
         line 840                                                        -> out-of-range (file has 839 lines)      | the gate classifies it: false
after:   line 839                                                        -> out-of-range (file has 838 lines)      | the gate classifies it: false
         line 840                                                        -> out-of-range (file has 838 lines)      | the gate classifies it: false
```

## ⛔ Why this is not a blanket `length - 1`

A file that does **not** end in a newline has no trailing empty element, and its real last line is exactly the one a blanket subtraction would delete. `wc -l` *undercounts* such a file, so "match `wc -l`" is not the rule either — the rule is "drop the terminator, if there is one". This tree contains such files, so the direction is not hypothetical; a test pins it, and that test is green on **both** sides of the repair, which is what makes it a control rather than a second copy of the fix.

Exactly one element is popped, which is also the right answer for a file ending in a blank line: that file has a genuinely empty last line **and** a terminator, and only the terminator goes.

## The two red-first assertions triage required

Both were run against the unrepaired boundary first — the repair committed, then `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` restored to `2bc9829ea` (on-disk hash proven equal to the base blob, `fileLines` occurrences 0), the suite run, then restored to `HEAD` (hash proven equal to the `HEAD` blob, `git diff HEAD` empty).

```
RED (unrepaired boundary):  Tests  5 failed | 62 passed (67)
  × reports a trailing-newline file at its `wc -l` length, not one more
      AssertionError: expected 5 to be 4
  × calls a citation AT the phantom line out of range, not non-substantive
      AssertionError: expected 'non-substantive' to be 'out-of-range'
  × drops the terminator of a file ending in a blank line, and nothing else
  × gives an empty file zero lines, so every citation into it is out of range
  × separates a line terminator from a line, in the helper itself
  ✓ keeps the real last line of a file that does NOT end in a newline   ← the control, green here too

GREEN (repaired):           Tests  67 passed (67)
```

⚠️ The cases go through **real files on disk**. Every pre-existing `judge` case hands it a pre-seeded `fileCache` holding an array someone already split, so those cases walk straight past this boundary and pass identically on the defect and on the fix. Only a read exercises it.

## One file edited, two readers verified

`scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` imports `judge` from the census and calls it, so the boundary is its boundary too and it is repaired with no line of it edited.

- `scripts/__tests__/cross-file-line-citation-census.test.ts` — 67 passed
- `scripts/__tests__/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.test.ts` — 40 passed
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` — `0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0`
- `pnpm census:cross-file-line-citations` — `✓ 11 of 11 control(s) passed -- this run IS a reading.`

## No headline count moves — measured on this tree, not argued

`--json --list-all` before and after, same tree:

| reading | before | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| population | 1273 | 1273 |
| rows whose **verdict** changed | — | **0** |
| `out-of-range` / `non-substantive` / `drifted` / `resolves` / … | identical | identical |
| both content-addressed controls | pass | pass |
| `out-of-range` rows whose printed `(file has N lines)` was corrected | — | **26 of 26** |

`out-of-range` and `non-substantive` are both members of `FALSE_VERDICTS` in the census and both map to `'false'` through `classify` in the gate, so nothing that counts treats them differently.

## ⭐ The ref-vs-file byte paragraph, preserved as triage ordered

The card set two byte readings of `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` side by side — **38980** at ref `a0176176a`, from the hand-back it was filed from, and **39757** at `origin/main` at filing time — and stated why the conclusion is unaffected: the LF count, `wc -l` and the split length were identical across both. Verbatim from the card: *"the byte figure is a reading of a **ref**, not a property of the file, and inheriting it would have published a number this seat did not take."*

That paragraph came true a **third** time while this card was in flight. Re-measured here on `main` = `2bc9829ea`, that same file reads **41893 bytes / 838 LF / `wc -l` 838 / split 839, last element still the empty string** — objectui#9898 merged into it after the card was filed. Three byte figures, one finding, unmoved: split still exceeds LF by exactly one and the last element is still empty.

## Optional escalation reading — report only, ⛔ not a grading

Triage set a mechanical escalation to p2: one real out-of-range citation in the tree that this off-by-one currently lets through. Run over today's tree, across all 957 population rows that resolve to a cited path:

**Citations landing exactly on the phantom line `wc -l` + 1: 0.** No false negative has occurred. Independently confirmed by the before/after diff above — 0 rows changed verdict. ⛔ This seat reports the reading and does not grade it.

## Scope

One boundary, as dispatched. `scanFile` (which iterates the **citing** file and publishes no length), the anchor scan, and `scripts/dollar-dialect-alias-census.mjs` all keep their `split('\n')`: they publish no file length and a phantom `''` matches no anchor.

Tooling and tests only; no package is released by this change.
